findingStatus.evidence: R-01 reproduction (all long runs of weeks 2-11 missed): race day EASY_CONVERSATIONAL completion. EVENT_AMBITIOUS_FOR_CURRENT_RUNNING is on every proposal from week 6, with options later or shorter first and caution LATER_OR_SHORTER_EVENT_FIRST; it names the windowed long run (70 at week 6, 0 at week 11) and says earlier long runs are too long ago to count. The taper long runs follow the window (45/35 = that week's easy runs when none is inside). Amendment 2's 'to verify' list: the fully executed reference keeps MARATHON_EFFORT (taper 125/100); the athlete missing only the last two specific long runs keeps MARATHON_EFFORT (window holds 175 at day -35; taper 120/95). Further probes: missing weeks 7-9 keeps effort (170 at -42); missing weeks 5-9 gives a completion (no long run on days 21-50); Monday and Wednesday races, 4 run days, and 150 min available all keep effort. The 10K and the half are byte-identical to 2d089c0 (16/16).

Proposals rebuild the projection: week 3 says 175 (projected weeks counted as executed); from week 6 the completion note replaces it. The creation note adds 'Race day is decided by the longest long run you complete between about 7 and 3 weeks before the race' (Amendment 2 disclosure).
Monday race: day -20 2x18' (0.6), day -13 2x15' (0.5). Races on Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday and Sunday give 0.6 then 0.5.
Post-race light strength through day 14 is at least 7 days apart: strength days [0,4] give 5, 12; [0,2,4] give 5, 12; [1,5] give 6, 13; [2] gives 10. The next block starts on day 15 or later.
With 4 run days the block notes add the weekly-share sentence; with 5 days they do not.
The walk/jog 5K athlete and a novice with 2 run days no longer get the threshold note; a novice with 3 run days does.
B2 now reads 'do not train for 7 days after it, and report those days as a break'.

newFindings.title: The marathon completion note opens with a contradictory clause
newFindings.reproduction: R-01 reproduction, any proposal from week 6: 'By race week the plan reaches a longest continuous run of 150 minutes, and its executed long run is below 150 minutes…' The first clause states the program's longest continuous run (the R6 template); the second sentence correctly gives the windowed value (70 or 0) and why.
newFindings.smallestFix: For the windowed basis, open with the windowed long run (e.g. 'Your longest long run between about 7 and 3 weeks before the race is N minutes, below 150…') or drop the continuous-run clause. Copy only; no dose.

regressionCheck.fiveK: No regression: planned sessions and decisions identical to 2d089c0 for 10 inputs (reference, novice, months 5, 2 and 4 run days, walk/jog, restart, Monday race, 8-week plan, missed and adverse script). Only change: the intended R-06 note removal for walk/jog.
regressionCheck.normalJourneys: No regression: profiles A-E, G and the 10K 8-week plan, with missed, partial and adverse scripts, give byte-identical final programs and decisions to 2d089c0.
regressionCheck.F08Cut: No regression on the V1 engine: a sign-free report and a check give KEEP with the typed unavailability; a later review with missed sessions is GATED_NEXT_STEP (no debt); any yes is CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED; an unanswered or non-boolean sign is asked; the hold survives an omitted reference, a return, a goal change and RECOVERED; only a clean readiness declaration releases it, sport by sport, into the same conservative entry (15-min easy runs, 1 set at RIR 4). QRE-V1FC-02: an unknown condition is now asked by name; an unrecognized sign key is asked; a yes beside an unrecognized key still routes to the clinical hold (precedence kept); intent, days, region and sports are not asked, which is correct since V1 does not read them.

otherJudgesSportingSide.SEC-V1FC-03: Coherent: a missed session of the current week that is already past is handled as before (KEEP, nothing moved); a session of the previous week or one still ahead is asked about, nothing is moved or copied. No make-up path is created.
otherJudgesSportingSide.QRE-V1FC-01: Coherent: a later marathon date asks for a new plan (where B1 is read again); the same marathon keeps the plan; a switch from the marathon to the half re-plans future phases as the R6 half does; a 10K date change is unchanged.
